origins: Racing thoughts, panic, intrusive images, flashbacks, or strange sensations can be frightening and make us fear losing our minds. Fear of “going crazy” often intensifies the very symptoms, and secrecy deepens it.
teaches: God has not given us “a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control” (2 Timothy 1:7). “When anxiety overwhelms me, Your consolation delights my soul.” “You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.” “Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.” Anxiety and distress are among the most common human experiences, and they are treatable. They do not mean you are losing your mind. Tell a doctor or counselor right away if symptoms are severe or frightening.
self_statements: Something terrible is happening in my head.
If anyone knew they would lock me up.
errors: Believing I am either sane or going crazy.
Predicting that I will lose control.
Feeling terrified and concluding that I am going crazy.
questions: Has a doctor or counselor evaluated these symptoms?
How often do these fears come true?
What helps calm my body, like slow breathing or prayer?
What does Scripture say about God’s gift of a sound mind?
truth: These experiences are frightening but common and treatable. God gives power, love, and self-control, and I can seek help right away. I am not alone.
hw_truths: God gives me power, love, and self-control.
He keeps me in perfect peace.
log: Each week, note one step you took for calm and one person you told.
